newsitem.title: USA: Delta sees stronger than expected growth.
newsitem.headline: Delta sees stronger than expected growth.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc said Monday it expects stronger than previously anticipated growth in September revenues, more than offsetting cost increases.
"Our record traffic performance for August exceeded our expectations," said Chief Financial Officer Thomas Roeck.
The airline said its system load factor for August was 77.69 percent, compared to 70.43 percent in August 1995.
Revenue passenger miles jumped 13.3 percent in August to 9.04 billion on a 2.7 percent increase in capacity.

"While our August results reflect continued downward pressure on passenger mile yields due to the increase in leisure-oriented traffic, we now expect to report stronger growth in unit revenues for the September 1996 quarter than we had previously anticipated," Roeck said.

He also said that for its fiscal first quarter, ended September 30, incremental traffic is expected to increase volume and revenue-related unit costs by about $0.001 per available seat mile, and recent fuel price increases are expected to increase unit costs by another $0.001.

He said higher than anticipated expenses in other cost categories, primarily marketing and security costs related to the 1996 Olympic Games and higher booking fee payments, are expected to raise unit costs by an additional $0.0005 per available seat mile.
"As a result, we now expect unit costs for the September quarter to be $0.087 per available seat mile.
"We do, however, anticipate that the unit cost increases will be more than offset by higher unit revenues, contributing positively toward achievement of our operating margin goals," said Roeck.
